title: Why It Slid? Limiting Friction Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A book on a tilted desk stays put, until one tilt too many. A sand pile never gets steeper than one slope. Something holds them, but only up to a limit. And when Aarav tilts his drawing board, his geometry box holds, holds, then shoots down at one exact angle, even with two boxes taped together. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we learn limiting friction: the largest static friction, just before slipping starts.

On a live motion notebook a 2 kg block sits on a tilting board with mu_s = 0.5. The readout and a friction vs angle graph move together: friction matches mg sin theta (3.4 N at 10 degrees, 6.7 N at 20) while the limit mu_s N shrinks, until they meet at 26.6 degrees and 8.8 N. Then the block slips and kinetic friction, about 7 N, takes over. A slow-mo replay freezes the moment of slipping. We derive tan theta_r = mu_s step by step, see link by link why the mass cancels, compare friction below and at the limit, meet the angle of repose and the angle of friction (and why they are equal), work out the smallest push that holds a book on a wall, see the exam trap, and solve an original JEE Main pattern question.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 It holds, up to a limit
0:25 What limiting friction is: f_L = mu_s N
0:44 Motion notebook: the tilting board
1:20 Slow-mo replay: the moment of slipping
1:32 The rule: tan theta_r = mu_s, step by step
2:14 Why the mass cancels, link by link
2:30 Below the limit vs at the limit + pause and think
3:02 Angle of repose vs angle of friction + pause and think
3:40 Worked example: a book pressed on a wall
4:15 Exam trap: mu_s, not mu_k
4:35 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:15 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Rolling Friction. Why is a heavy box so much easier to move on wheels?
